questions.question: John drives 250 km at 50 km/h and then he drives 350 km at 70 km/h. Find his average speed for the whole journey in km/h.
questions.questionHtml: John drives 250 km at 50 km/h and then he drives 350 km at 70 km/h. Find his average speed for the whole journey in km/h.
questions.solution:
Time taken to cover first distance = 250 / 50 = 5 h

Time taken to cover second distance = 350 / 70 = 5 h

⇒ Average speed = (250 + 350) / (5 + 5) = 600 / 10 = 60 km/h

questions.question: A bus covers a certain distance travelling at a speed of 40 km/h and returns to the starting point at a speed of 60 km/h. The average speed (in km/h) for the entire journey is:
questions.questionHtml: A bus covers a certain distance travelling at a speed of 40 km/h and returns to the starting point at a speed of 60 km/h. The average speed (in km/h) for the entire journey is:
questions.solution:
Total Time taken = ( d/40 + d/60) h = d/24 h

Average = Total Distance / Total time = 2d ÷ (d/24) = 48 km/h.

questions.question: A person travels in a car at 40 km/h for 3 hours, on a bike at 30 km/h for 2 hours, and in a train at 80 km/h for 5 hours. What is the average speed at which he travelled?
questions.questionHtml: A person travels in a car at 40 km/h for 3 hours, on a bike at 30 km/h for 2 hours, and in a train at 80 km/h for 5 hours. What is the average speed at which he travelled?
questions.solution:
Distance traveled by car = 3 x 40 = 120 km, by bike = 2 x 30 = 60 km, and by train = 5 x 80 = 400 km

Total time taken = 10 hours, Total distance = 580 km

Average speed = Total distance / Total time = \(\frac{580}{10}\) = 58 km/h

questions.question: A jeep travels to a place 300 km away at an average speed of 60 km/h and returns at a speed of 30 km/h. What is the average speed (in km/h) for the whole journey?
questions.questionHtml: A jeep travels to a place 300 km away at an average speed of 60 km/h and returns at a speed of 30 km/h. What is the average speed (in km/h) for the whole journey?
questions.solution:
If distance is constant, then average speed = \(\frac{2S_1 S_2}{S_1 + S_2}\) [ whereS1 and S2 are speed]

Here, the traveled distance is the same i.e. 300 km.

The average speed for the whole journey ⇒ (2 × 60 × 30) ÷ (60 + 30) ⇒ 3600 ÷ 90 ⇒ 40 km/h

questions.question: A bus covers 1200 km in 30 hours. What is its average speed in m/s?
questions.questionHtml: A bus covers 1200 km in 30 hours. What is its average speed in m/s?
questions.solution:
Average Speed = Total Distance / Total Time

Average Speed (in km/h) = 1200 km / 30 hours, Average Speed = 40 km/h

Average Speed (in m/s) = (40 × 1000) / 3600, Average Speed ≈ \(11 \frac{1}{9}\) m/s

questions.question: A ship sails out to a mark at the speed of 15 km/h and sails back to the starting point at the speed of 10 km/h. The average speed of sailing of the ship is:
questions.questionHtml: A ship sails out to a mark at the speed of 15 km/h and sails back to the starting point at the speed of 10 km/h. The average speed of sailing of the ship is:
questions.solution: Average speed = \(\frac{2\times 15\times 10}{15+10}\) = \(\frac{300}{25}\) = 12 km/h

questions.question: A car covers the first 210 km at a speed of 70 km/h. It covered the next 170 km at a speed of 85 km/h. What is its average speed?
questions.questionHtml: A car covers the first 210 km at a speed of 70 km/h. It covered the next 170 km at a speed of 85 km/h. What is its average speed?
questions.solution: Average speed = (210 + 170)/{(210/70) + (170/85)} ⇒ 380/{3 + 2} ⇒ 380/5 = 76 km/h

questions.question: A car covers a distance of 350 km in 5 hours and covers another 450 km at a speed of 90 km/h. What is the average speed (in km/h) of the car?
questions.questionHtml: A car covers a distance of 350 km in 5 hours and covers another 450 km at a speed of 90 km/h. What is the average speed (in km/h) of the car?
questions.solution:
Total distance covered = 350 km + 450 km = 800 km

Total time = 5 hour + 5 hour = 10 hours

Average speed = Total distance/ Total time = 800/10 = 80 km/hr

questions.question: Shankar covers a certain distance by a car driving at 40 km/h and he returns to the starting point riding on a scooter with a speed of 20 km/h. Find the average speed of the whole journey.
questions.questionHtml: Shankar covers a certain distance by a car driving at 40 km/h and he returns to the starting point riding on a scooter with a speed of 20 km/h. Find the average speed of the whole journey.
questions.solution:
Average speed = Total distance / Total Time

Let distance one way = d ⇒ Time by car = d / 40

Time by scooter = d / 20 ⇒  Total Distance = 2d

Total Time = (d / 40) + (d / 20) = d(1/40 + 1/20) = d(1/40 + 2/40) = 3d /40

Average Speed = (2d) / (3d / 40) = (2d * 40) / 3d = 80d / 3d = 80 / 3 =

262/3 km/h

questions.question: A car covered the first 100 km at a speed of 50 km/h. It covered next 140 km at a speed of 70 km/h. What is its average speed?
questions.questionHtml: A car covered the first 100 km at a speed of 50 km/h. It covered next 140 km at a speed of 70 km/h. What is its average speed?
questions.solution:
Car covered first 100km at a speed of 50km/h so, time taken = 100/50 = 2 h

Now, Next 140 km at speed of 70km/h, so time taken = 140/70 = 2 

Total distance = ( 100 + 140 ) = 240km and total time taken = 2 h 

Average speed = (Total distance/Total time) = 240 /4 = 60km/h

questions.question: A car travels the first 180 km at a speed of 20 km/h. It covers the next 210 km at a speed of 35 km/h. Find the average speed of the car (in km/h).
questions.questionHtml: A car travels the first 180 km at a speed of 20 km/h. It covers the next 210 km at a speed of 35 km/h. Find the average speed of the car (in km/h).
questions.solution:
Time (T1) = 180 /20 = 9 hours

Time (T2) = 210/35 = 6 hours  

Total Distance = 180 km + 210 km = 390 km 

Total Time = 9 hours + 6 hours = 15 hours

Average Speed = Total Distance / Total Time

⇒ 390 km / 15 hours  = 26 km/h

questions.question: A man walks from point X to Y at a speed of 20 km/h, but comes back from point Y to X at a speed of 25 km/h. Find his average speed.
questions.questionHtml: A man walks from point X to Y at a speed of 20 km/h, but comes back from point Y to X at a speed of 25 km/h. Find his average speed.
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

When the distance traveled is the same (X to Y and Y to X), Average Speed = [2 × a × b] ÷ [a + b].

Average Speed = [2 × 20 × 25] ÷ [20 + 25] = 1000 ÷ 45.

Average Speed = 200 ÷ 9 = 22 2/9 km/h.

∴ The correct answer is 22 2/9 km/h.

Alternate Method

Given: Speed from X to Y (v1) = 20 km/h, Speed from Y to X (v2) = 25 km/h.

Formula Used: Average Speed = Total Distance ÷ Total Time

⇒ Let the distance between X and Y be the LCM of 20 and 25, which is 100 km.

⇒ Time taken from X to Y (t1) = 100 ÷ 20 = 5 hours.

⇒ Time taken from Y to X (t2) = 100 ÷ 25 = 4 hours.

⇒ Total distance = 100 + 100 = 200 km.

⇒ Total time = 5 + 4 = 9 hours.

⇒ Average Speed = 200 ÷ 9 = 22 2/9 km/h.

∴ The correct answer is 22 2/9 km/h.

Additional Information

Average Speed for Equal Time

If a person travels for equal time intervals at speeds v1 and v2, then the Average Speed = (v1 + v2) ÷ 2.

Relative Speed

When two objects move in opposite directions, their relative speed is the sum of their individual speeds (u + v). When in the same direction, it is the difference (u − v).

Average Speed for Three Equal Distances

If three equal distances are covered at speeds a, b, and c, then Average Speed = (3 × a × b × c) ÷ (ab + bc + ca).

questions.question: A man goes from place A to B at a speed of 12 km/h and returns from B to A at a speed of 18 km/h. His average speed for the entire journey is:
questions.questionHtml: A man goes from place A to B at a speed of 12 km/h and returns from B to A at a speed of 18 km/h. His average speed for the entire journey is:
questions.solution:
Given:

A man goes from place A to B at a speed of 12 km/h

Returns from B to A at a speed of 18 km/h.

Formula Used:

Average speed = \(\frac{2xy}{x+y}\)

Calculations:

⇒ Speed from place A to B = 12 km/h

⇒ Speed from place B to A = 18 km/h

The average speed will be

⇒ Average speed = \(\frac{2xy}{x+y}=\frac{2\times 12 \times 18}{12 +18}=\frac{24\times 18}{30}=14\frac{2}{5}\) 

⇒ Hence, The average speed of the man will be 14\(\frac{2}{5}\) km/h.

questions.question: Prasad goes 96 kilometres on a bike at a speed of 16 km/h, 124 kilometres at 31 km/h in a car, and 105 kilometres at 7 km/h in a horse cart. Find his average speed for the entire distance travelled.
questions.questionHtml: Prasad goes 96 kilometres on a bike at a speed of 16 km/h, 124 kilometres at 31 km/h in a car, and 105 kilometres at 7 km/h in a horse cart. Find his average speed for the entire distance travelled.
questions.solution:
Total distance  = 96 + 124 + 105 = 325 km

Total time = 96/16 + 124/31 + 105/7 = 6 + 4 + 15 = 25

Average speed = total distance/total time taken = 325/25 = 13 km/h

questions.question: A person covers a certain distance by bus at 45 km/h and immediately returns to the starting point by car at a speed of 80 km/h. What is his average speed during the whole journey?
questions.questionHtml: A person covers a certain distance by bus at 45 km/h and immediately returns to the starting point by car at a speed of 80 km/h. What is his average speed during the whole journey?
questions.solution:
If distance is constant, the average speed = \(\frac{2 \times S_1 \times S_2}{(S_1 + S_2)}\) [ where S1 and S2 are two speeds ]

Average speed = \(\frac{2 \times 45 \times 80}{(45 + 80)}\) = 288/5 = 57.6 km/hr

questions.question: A motorcyclist rides his motorcycle at a speed of 90 km/hr in the first one hour and the next two hours at a speed of 120 km/hr. Find the average speed of the rider.
questions.questionHtml: A motorcyclist rides his motorcycle at a speed of 90 km/hr in the first one hour and the next two hours at a speed of 120 km/hr. Find the average speed of the rider.
questions.solution:
Given: Speed in the first hour = 90 km/hr Speed in the next two hours = 120 km/hr

 

Distance1 = 90 km/hr × 1 hr = 90 km Distance2 = 120 km/hr × 2 hr = 240 km

 

Total distance = 90 km + 240 km = 330 km Total time = 1 hr + 2 hr = 3 hr

 

Average speed = 330 km / 3 hr = 110 km/hr

questions.question: A bus travels for three hours at 60 km/h, four hours at 50 km/h and the next five hours at 50 km/h. Find its average speed.
questions.questionHtml: A bus travels for three hours at 60 km/h, four hours at 50 km/h and the next five hours at 50 km/h. Find its average speed.
questions.solution:
Total distance covered by bus in (3 + 4 + 5) hours  = (60 × 3) + (4 × 50) + (5 × 50) = (180 + 200 + 250) km = 630 km

Average speed = 630/12 = 52.5 km/h

questions.question: A man covers the first 210 km of a journey at 60 km/h and the next 198 km at 66 km/h. The average speed for the whole journey is:
questions.questionHtml: A man covers the first 210 km of a journey at 60 km/h and the next 198 km at 66 km/h. The average speed for the whole journey is:
questions.solution:
Time taken to cover 210 km distance at 60 km/hr = 210/60 = 3.5 hr

Time taken to cover 198 km distance at 66 km/hr = 198/66 = 3 hr

As we know,

Average speed = Total distance/total time = (210 + 198) / (3.5 + 3) = 62.8 km/hr

questions.question: A cyclist rides 20 km in 120 minutes and rides another 25 km in 150 minutes. What is the average speed of the cyclist, in km/h?
questions.questionHtml: A cyclist rides 20 km in 120 minutes and rides another 25 km in 150 minutes. What is the average speed of the cyclist, in km/h?
questions.solution:
Total distance is 20 + 25 = 45 km

Total time is 150 + 120 = 270 minutes

270 minutes = 4 hr and 30 minutes 

Average speed is  45 /4.5 = 10 km/h

questions.question: A man divided his journey into three parts of distances of 18 km, 20 km, and 27 km. He travelled the distances at the speeds of 6 km/h, 5 km/h, and 9 km/h, respectively. What was his average speed during the entire journey?
questions.questionHtml: A man divided his journey into three parts of distances of 18 km, 20 km, and 27 km. He travelled the distances at the speeds of 6 km/h, 5 km/h, and 9 km/h, respectively. What was his average speed during the entire journey?
questions.solution:
Calculation:

Time taken by man to cover 18 km distance at the speed of 6 km/hr. = 18/6 = 3 hrs.

Time taken by man to cover 20 km distance at the speed of 5 km/hr. = 20/5 = 4 hrs.

Time taken by man to cover 27 km distance at the speed of 9 km/hr. = 27/9 = 3 hrs.

Total distance = 18 + 20 + 27 = 65 km

Total time = 3 + 4 + 3 = 10 hrs.

∴ Average speed = 65/10 = 6.5 km/hr.

questions.question: A person travels from P to Q at a speed of 50 km/h and returns by increasing his speed by 60%. What is his average speed for both the trips?
questions.questionHtml: A person travels from P to Q at a speed of 50 km/h and returns by increasing his speed by 60%. What is his average speed for both the trips?
questions.solution:
Speed at time of returning = 50 × 160% ⇒ 80 km/h

Average speed = (2 × 50 × 80)/(50 + 80) ⇒ 61.53 km/h

questions.question: The distance between two stations, A and B, is 428 km. a train starts from station ‘A’ at 6:00 a.m and moves towards station ‘B’ at an average speed of 48 km/h. Another train starts from station ‘B’ at 6:20 a.m and moves towards statin ‘A’ at an average speed of 55 km/h. At what time will the trains meet?
questions.questionHtml: The distance between two stations, A and B, is 428 km. a train starts from station ‘A’ at 6:00 a.m and moves towards station ‘B’ at an average speed of 48 km/h. Another train starts from station ‘B’ at 6:20 a.m and moves towards statin ‘A’ at an average speed of 55 km/h. At what time will the trains meet?
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Train A travels alone for 20 minutes (1/3 hour) → Distance = 48 × (1/3) = 16 km.

Remaining distance at 6:20 a.m. = 428 − 16 = 412 km.

Relative speed = 48 + 55 = 103 km/h.

Time to meet = 412 ÷ 103 = 4 hours after 6:20 a.m.

∴ The correct answer is 10:20 a.m.

Alternate Method

Given: Total Distance = 428 km, Speed of Train A = 48 km/h (starts 6:00 a.m.), Speed of Train B = 55 km/h (starts 6:20 a.m.).

Formula Used: Distance = Speed × Time; Relative Speed (Opposite direction) = S1 + S2.

⇒ Distance covered by Train A in 20 mins = 48 × (20/60) = 16 km.

⇒ Distance between trains at 6:20 a.m. = 428 − 16 = 412 km.

⇒ Relative speed = 48 + 55 = 103 km/h.

⇒ Time taken to meet = 412 ÷ 103 = 4 hours.

⇒ Meeting time = 6:20 a.m. + 4 hours = 10:20 a.m.

∴ The correct answer is 10:20 a.m.

Additional Information

Relative Speed Concept

When two objects move toward each other, their relative speed is the sum of their individual speeds: Srel = S1 + S2.

Meeting Time Rule

To calculate meeting time, ensure both objects start moving from their respective positions at the same reference time by calculating initial distance covered.

Unit Conversion

Always convert time into hours when speed is in km/h: 1 minute = 1/60 hour.

questions.question: A cyclist rides 10 km at an average speed of 15 km/hr and then the next 15 km at an average speed of 10 km/hr. The average speed of the entire ride is:
questions.questionHtml: A cyclist rides 10 km at an average speed of 15 km/hr and then the next 15 km at an average speed of 10 km/hr. The average speed of the entire ride is:
questions.solution:
Given:

A cyclist rides 10 km at an average speed of 15 km/hr and then the next 15 km at an average speed of 10 km/hr.

Formula used:

Average Speed = Total Distance / Total Time

Calculation:

First part:

Distance1 = 10 km

Speed1 = 15 km/hr

Time1 = Distance1 / Speed1

⇒ Time1 = 10 / 15

⇒ Time1 = 2/3 hr

Second part:

Distance2 = 15 km

Speed2 = 10 km/hr

Time2 = Distance2 / Speed2

⇒ Time2 = 15 / 10

⇒ Time2 = 1.5 hr

Total Distance = Distance1 + Distance2

⇒ Total Distance = 10 + 15

⇒ Total Distance = 25 km

Total Time = Time1 + Time2

⇒ Total Time = 2/3 + 1.5

⇒ Total Time = 2/3 + 3/2

⇒ Total Time = 4/6 + 9/6

⇒ Total Time = 13/6 hr

Average Speed = Total Distance / Total Time

⇒ Average Speed = 25 / (13/6)

⇒ Average Speed = 25 × 6/13

⇒ Average Speed = 150/13

⇒ Average Speed ≈ 11.54 km/hr

∴ The correct answer is option (3).

questions.question: A truck covers three equal distances of 100 km at the speed of 200 km/hr, 300 km/hr and 600 km/hr. Find the average speed of the truck for the whole journey.
questions.questionHtml: A truck covers three equal distances of 100 km at the speed of 200 km/hr, 300 km/hr and 600 km/hr. Find the average speed of the truck for the whole journey.
questions.solution:
For the first distance of 100 km at a speed of 200 km/hr, Time taken = 100 km / 200 km/hr = 1/2 hr

For the second distance of 100 km at a speed of 300 km/hr, Time taken = 100 km/300 km/hr = 1/3 hr

For the third distance of 100 km at a speed of 600 km/hr, Time taken = 100 km / 600 km/hr = 1/6 hr

Total distance = 100 km + 100 km + 100 km = 300 km

Total time = 1/2 hr + 1/3 hr + 1/6 hr = 1, Average speed = 300 km/hr

questions.question: The average run rate of a cricket team during the first 20 overs is 4.5. What should be the asking rate per over for the next 30 overs, if it has to chase a target of 282 runs in total?
questions.questionHtml: The average run rate of a cricket team during the first 20 overs is 4.5. What should be the asking rate per over for the next 30 overs, if it has to chase a target of 282 runs in total?
questions.solution:
Total runs in 50 overs = 282

Average of runs in 20 overs = 4.5

Sum of run in 20 overs = 4.5 × 20 = 90

Runs need in remaining 30 overs = 282 - 90 = 192

Average runs in 30 overs = 192/30 = 6.4

questions.question: Richa travels from A to B at the speed of 15 km/h, from B to C at 20 km/h, and from C to D at 30 km/h If AB = BC = CD, then find the Richa's average speed.
questions.questionHtml: Richa travels from A to B at the speed of 15 km/h, from B to C at 20 km/h, and from C to D at 30 km/h If AB = BC = CD, then find the Richa's average speed.
questions.solution:
Calculation:

Let AB = BC = CD = 60 km (LCM of 15, 20 and 30)

Total distance = 3 × 60 = 180 km

Time taken by Richa to travels from A to B = 60/15 = 4 hrs.

Time taken by Richa to travels from B to C = 60/20 = 3 hrs.

Time taken by Richa to travels from C to D = 60/30 = 2 hrs.

Total time taken by Richa to travels from A to D = 4 + 3 + 2 = 9 hrs.

∴ Average speed = 180/9 = 20 km/hr.

questions.question: A boy goes from home to school at a speed of 30 km/h and returns back at a speed of 70 km/h. What is his average speed for the journey?
questions.questionHtml: A boy goes from home to school at a speed of 30 km/h and returns back at a speed of 70 km/h. What is his average speed for the journey?
questions.solution:
Average speed  = \(\frac{2ab}{a+b}\)

⇒ Average speed = \(\frac{2\times 30\times 70}{30 + 70}\) ⇒ \(\frac{4200}{100}\) ⇒ 42 km/hr

questions.question: Priya covers a certain distance by her car at a speed of 21 km/h and returns at a speed of 17 km/h. What is her average speed during the travel?
questions.questionHtml: Priya covers a certain distance by her car at a speed of 21 km/h and returns at a speed of 17 km/h. What is her average speed during the travel?
questions.solution: Average speed = \(\frac{2\times 21\times17}{21+17}=\frac{714}{38}=18\frac{15}{19}\) km/h

questions.question: A person divides his total route of journey into three equal parts and decides to travel the three parts at the speeds of 80 km/h, 60 km/h and 30 km/h, respectively. What is the average speed during the journey?
questions.questionHtml: A person divides his total route of journey into three equal parts and decides to travel the three parts at the speeds of 80 km/h, 60 km/h and 30 km/h, respectively. What is the average speed during the journey?
questions.solution:
Total distance = 3D, Time = D/80 + D/60 + D/30 = D(1/80 + 1/60 + 1/30)

Total time = D(3/240 + 4/240 + 8/240) = D/16

Average Speed = 3D / (D/16) = 48 km/h

questions.question: Gopal travels from A to B at the speed of 5 km/h, from B to C at 10 km/h, and from C to D at 15 km/h. If AB = BC = CD, then find Gopal’s average speed.
questions.questionHtml: Gopal travels from A to B at the speed of 5 km/h, from B to C at 10 km/h, and from C to D at 15 km/h. If AB = BC = CD, then find Gopal’s average speed.
questions.solution:
AB = BC = CD  = x, then time to travel A to B = x/5 h, Time to travel B to C = x/ 10 h and time to travel C to D = x/15 h

Total Distance travelled = AB + BC + CD = ( x + x + x) = 3x km

Total Time taken = ( x/5 + x/10 +x/15) = 11x/30 hours

Average Speed = 3x/( 11x /30) = ( 3x × 30/11x) = 90/11 = \(8 \frac{2}{11}\) km/h

questions.question: In a Hindi test of 100 marks, 11 students got 78 marks, 7 students got 80 marks, 5 students got 82 marks and 2 students got 86 marks. What was the average marks in Hindi?
questions.questionHtml: In a Hindi test of 100 marks, 11 students got 78 marks, 7 students got 80 marks, 5 students got 82 marks and 2 students got 86 marks. What was the average marks in Hindi?
questions.solution:
Given:

Hindi test of 100 marks

11 students got 78 marks

7 students got 80 marks

5 students got 82 marks

2 students got 86 marks

Formula Used:

Average= \(\frac{Sum \space of \space marks}{Total \space students}\)

Calculations:

According to the question,

11 students got 78 marks

⇒ Average= \(\frac{Sum \space of \space marks}{Total \space students}\)

⇒ Sum of marks= Average x Total Marks= 11 x 78= 858 marks

7 students got 80 marks

⇒ Average= \(\frac{Sum \space of \space marks}{Total \space students}\)

⇒ Sum of marks= Average x Total Marks= 7 x 80= 560 marks

5 students got 82 marks

⇒ Average= \(\frac{Sum \space of \space marks}{Total \space students}\)

⇒ Sum of marks= Average x Total Marks= 5 x 82= 410 marks

2 students got 86 marks

⇒ Average= \(\frac{Sum \space of \space marks}{Total \space students}\)

⇒ Sum of marks= Average x Total Marks= 2 x 86= 172 marks

Average marks on Hindi test,

⇒ Average= \(\frac{Sum \space of \space marks}{Total \space students}=\frac{858+560+410+172}{11+7+5+2}=\frac{2000}{25}\)= 80

Hence, The average mark on the Hindi test is 80

questions.question: Akhil rides first 12 km at a speed of 16 km/h and further 6 km at a speed of 20 km/h. Find his average speed (in km/h).
questions.questionHtml: Akhil rides first 12 km at a speed of 16 km/h and further 6 km at a speed of 20 km/h. Find his average speed (in km/h).
questions.solution:
Total distance covered = 12 + 6 = 18 km

Time taken for 12 km ride = \(12\over16\) hr

Time taken for 6 km ride = \(6\over20\) hr

Total time = \(12\over16\) + \(6\over20\) = \(84\over80\) hr

Average speed = \(18\over{84\over 80}\) = 18 × \(80\over84\) = 17\(1\over7\) km/h

questions.question: If a truck moves at a constant speed of 30 km/h for 1 kilometre and 45 km/h for the next 1 kilometre. What is the average speed of the truck?
questions.questionHtml: If a truck moves at a constant speed of 30 km/h for 1 kilometre and 45 km/h for the next 1 kilometre. What is the average speed of the truck?
questions.solution:
Total Distance = 2 km, Total time = 1/30 + 1/45 = 5/90

Average Speed = 2/5 × 90 = 2 × 18 = 36 kmhr

questions.question: Ramesh, on his way to his hometown, travelled the first 250 km at a speed of 75 km/h and the next 250 km at a speed of 85 km/h. Find the average speed for the whole journey(correct to 2 decimal places).
questions.questionHtml: Ramesh, on his way to his hometown, travelled the first 250 km at a speed of 75 km/h and the next 250 km at a speed of 85 km/h. Find the average speed for the whole journey(correct to 2 decimal places).
questions.solution:
Time Speed Distance
17 75 1275
15 85

Average speed = (1275 × 2)/(17 + 15) ⇒ 2550/32 = 1275/16 = 79.68 km/h

questions.question: The driver of a car travelling at a speed of 60 km/h decides to slow down to 40 km/h after covering half of the distance. What is the average speed of the car (in km/h)?
questions.questionHtml: The driver of a car travelling at a speed of 60 km/h decides to slow down to 40 km/h after covering half of the distance. What is the average speed of the car (in km/h)?
questions.solution:
Time Speed Distance
2 60 120
3 40

Average speed =  (120 × 2)/5 = 48 km/h

questions.question: Mohan travels three equal distances at speeds of 12 km/h, 18 km/h and 24 km/h. If he takes a total of 13 hours, then what is the total distance covered?
questions.questionHtml: Mohan travels three equal distances at speeds of 12 km/h, 18 km/h and 24 km/h. If he takes a total of 13 hours, then what is the total distance covered?
questions.solution:
Calculation:

∵ Mohan travels 3 equal distance with different speed.

 Let, the equal distance travel = a km

∴ (a/12) + (a/18) + (a/24) = 13

Taking LCM of 12, 18 and 24, we get 72.

∴ (6a/72) + (4a/72) + (3a/72) = 13

⇒ (6a + 4a + 3a)/72 = 13

⇒ 13a/72 = 13

⇒ a = (13 × 72)/13

⇒ a = 72 km

∴ Total distance travelled by him = a + a + a

= 3 × 72 = 216 km

questions.question: A person drives 110 miles at 55 miles per hour, he drives the next 120 miles at 60 miles per hour, and then he drives the next 60 miles in an hour. What is his average speed for the entire journey in miles per hour ?
questions.questionHtml: A person drives 110 miles at 55 miles per hour, he drives the next 120 miles at 60 miles per hour, and then he drives the next 60 miles in an hour. What is his average speed for the entire journey in miles per hour ?
questions.solution:
110 miles at 55 mph: time = 110 / 55 = 2 hours,

120 miles at 60 mph: time = 120 / 60 = 2 hours, 60 miles: time = 1 hour

Total distance = 290 miles, Total time = 5 hours,

Average speed = 290 / 5 = 58 mph

questions.question: A travels for 8 hours at the rate of 4 km/h and for 4 hours at the rate of 8 km/h. The average speed of the journey (in km/h) is:
questions.questionHtml: A travels for 8 hours at the rate of 4 km/h and for 4 hours at the rate of 8 km/h. The average speed of the journey (in km/h) is:
questions.solution:
Total Distance = 8 × 4 + 4 × 8 = 32 + 32 = 64 km,

Total Time = 8 + 4 = 12 hours,

Average Speed = 64 km / 12 hours = \(5 \frac{1}{3}\) km/h

questions.question: The speed of a car going from A to B is 110 km/h, while coming back, its speed is 76 km/h. What is the average speed during the entire journey?
questions.questionHtml: The speed of a car going from A to B is 110 km/h, while coming back, its speed is 76 km/h. What is the average speed during the entire journey?
questions.solution: Average speed = 2 × (a × b)\(a + b) ⇒ 2 × (110 × 76)\(110 + 76)  ⇒ (110 × 76)/93 ⇒ 89(83/93)

questions.question: A car covers 15 km, 20 km, 30 km and 12 km at speeds of 20 km/h, 30 km/h, 40 km/h and 30 km/h respectively. The average speed of the car for the total journey is:
questions.questionHtml: A car covers 15 km, 20 km, 30 km and 12 km at speeds of 20 km/h, 30 km/h, 40 km/h and 30 km/h respectively. The average speed of the car for the total journey is:
questions.solution:
Given:

A car covers 15 km, 20 km, 30 km and 12 km at speeds of 20 km/h, 30 km/h, 40 km/h and 30 km/h respectively.

Formula Used:

Average Speed = Total distance/Total time taken

Time taken = Distance/Speed

Calculation:

Time taken to cover 15 km at speed of 20 km/hr = 15/20 = 3/4 hours

Time taken to cover 20 km at speed of 30 km/hr = 20/30 = 2/3 hours

Time taken to cover 30 km at speed of 40 km/hr = 30/40 = 3/4 hours

Time taken to cover 12 km at speed of 30 km/hr = 12/30 = 2/5 hours

Total time taken = 3/4 + 2/3 + 3/4 + 2/5 = (45 + 40 +45 + 24)/60 = 154/60 = 77/30

The total Distance = 15 + 20 + 30 + 12 = 77

The average speed =  77/77 × 30 = 30 km/hr

∴ The average speed of the car for total journey is 30km/hr.

questions.question: A man travels some distance from his house to the exhibition ground by an auto at a speed of 30 km/h and returns by a cab at a speed of 50 km/h. What is his average speed (in km/h)?
questions.questionHtml: A man travels some distance from his house to the exhibition ground by an auto at a speed of 30 km/h and returns by a cab at a speed of 50 km/h. What is his average speed (in km/h)?
questions.solution:
Given:

A man travels some distance from his house to the exhibition ground by an auto at a speed of 30 km/h and returns by a cab at a speed of 50 km/h.

Formula used:

Average Speed = \(\dfrac{2 \times \text{Speed}_1 \times \text{Speed}_2}{\text{Speed}_1 + \text{Speed}_2}\)

Calculations:

Average Speed = \(\dfrac{2 \times 30 \times 50}{30 + 50}\)

⇒ Average Speed = \(\dfrac{3000}{80}\)

⇒ Average Speed = 37.5 km/h

∴ The correct answer is option 1.

questions.question: Pawan travels from X to Y at the speed of 10 km/h, from Y to Z at 15 km/h and from Z to W at 20 km/h. If XY = YZ = ZW (in km), then the average speed of Pawan for the whole journey is:
questions.questionHtml: Pawan travels from X to Y at the speed of 10 km/h, from Y to Z at 15 km/h and from Z to W at 20 km/h. If XY = YZ = ZW (in km), then the average speed of Pawan for the whole journey is:
questions.solution:
Let each segment distance = d km. so,Total distance = 3d km

Time for XY = d/10, Time for YZ = d/15, Time for ZW = d/20

Total time = d/10 + d/15 + d/20 = d(1/10 + 1/15 + 1/20) = d(13/60)

Average speed = 3d/(d(13/60)) = 3 * 60/13 = 180/13

Average speed = 1311/13 km/h

questions.question: If a man travels at \(\frac{1}{x}\) km/h on a journey and returns at \(\rm \frac{1}{x^2}\) km/h, then his average speed for the journey is:
questions.questionHtml: If a man travels at \(\frac{1}{x}\) km/h on a journey and returns at \(\rm \frac{1}{x^2}\) km/h, then his average speed for the journey is:
questions.solution: Average speed = (2 × S1 × S2)/(S1 + S2) = \(\frac{2\times\frac{1}{x}\times\frac{1}{x^2}}{\frac{1}{x}+\frac{1}{x^2}}\) = \(\rm \frac{2}{x+x^2}\)

questions.question: Roshni travelled at the speed of 66 km/h while going from point A to point B and returned via the same route at the speed of 92.4 km/h . What was Roshni's overall average speed during the two-way journey?
questions.questionHtml: Roshni travelled at the speed of 66 km/h while going from point A to point B and returned via the same route at the speed of 92.4 km/h. What was Roshni's overall average speed during the two-way journey?
questions.solution:
Alternate Method

By using the formula,

Average speed = \(\frac{2ab}{a+b}\) , where a and b are going and returning speed

Average speed = \(\frac{2\times66\times92.4}{66+92.4}\)

By calculation,

Average speed = 77Km/hr

questions.question: A car travelled distances of 10 km, 20 km and 30 km at speeds of 30 km/h, 40 km/h and 60 km/h, respectively. The average speed of the car is:
questions.questionHtml: A car travelled distances of 10 km, 20 km and 30 km at speeds of 30 km/h, 40 km/h and 60 km/h, respectively. The average speed of the car is:
questions.solution: Average Speed of car = \(\frac{60}{\frac{1}{3}+\frac{1}{2}+\frac{1}{2}}=\frac{60}{1+\frac{1}{3}}\) ⇒ \(\frac{60}{\frac{4}{3}}=\frac{60\times 3}{4}=45km/h\)
